name: Visa-Free Entry / eVisa / Consular Visa

requirements.blocker_text: Nationals unilaterally exempted by Armenia, or exempted under a bilateral/multilateral agreement, may enter without a visa and stay up to 180 days within a one-year period (unless a specific agreement states otherwise).

requirement_groups.name: Holder of a US/EU/Schengen/GCC residence permit (temporary exemption, 1 Jul 2026 - 1 Jul 2027)

requirements.blocker_text: Nationals of 111 countries holding a valid residence permit from the US, EU, Schengen area, UAE, Bahrain, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, or Oman -- valid for at least 6 months from the date of entry -- may enter visa-free for up to 180 days within a one-year period, under a temporary exemption running 1 July 2026 to 1 July 2027.
requirements.fix_path: Obtain a valid residence permit from one of the listed jurisdictions, valid 6+ months from entry.

requirements.blocker_text: All other nationalities must obtain an eVisa via evisa.mfa.am or a consular visa; some nationalities can only obtain a visa upon invitation at a diplomatic mission. Standard visas are issued for a maximum of 120 days, extendable by another 60 days.
requirements.fix_path: Apply for an eVisa or consular visa.

evidence_required.document: Residence permit from a qualifying jurisdiction (temporary-exemption route)
eVisa application or invitation letter (other nationalities)

outcome.duration_length: 180 days within a 1-year period (visa-exempt/temporary-exemption); up to 120 days + 60-day extension (visa/eVisa)

sources.title: Armenian Ministry of Foreign Affairs -- visa policy: unilateral and bilateral/multilateral visa exemptions (180 days/year), a temporary 1 Jul 2026-1 Jul 2027 exemption for holders of US/EU/Schengen/GCC residence permits (111 countries), eVisa via evisa.mfa.am, standard visa 120+60 days, invitation-only nationalities

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Armenia). The exact list of unilaterally-exempt and bilaterally-exempt nationalities is published as separate lists on the MFA site rather than reproduced on the summary page fetched -- not reproduced here in full. The 111-country temporary exemption (distinct from the general unilateral/bilateral exemption) is time-bound (1 July 2026 - 1 July 2027) and modeled as its own requirement group since it is a genuinely separate, temporary legal basis, not a restatement of the general visa-free regime.
